records.rationale: One-off manual verification trade: confirms the place_spread_order code path, both hard backstops, and Alpaca order submission all work end-to-end before relying on it unattended.

QQQ bull call spread on Sep 2 expiry. QQQ reversed from pre-market weakness (~$714) to open strong at ~$716. The 50-delta strike at $716 confirms current price. Low IV (~19%) makes debit spreads cost-effective. The market absorbed selling pressure and opened at a bullish level vs Friday close. Targeting a move to $720+ by Wednesday. Spread width $4, debit ~$2.01, ~1:1 risk/reward with strong entry signal from opening reversal.

Closing the QQQ $716/$720C bull call spread. Two failed intraday rally attempts (bounces to $715.84-$715.90 both rejected). QQQ now back at $714.09-$714.29, showing lower highs pattern (717 → 715.90 → 714.10). Break-even at expiry requires QQQ at $717.76 — over $3.50 from current price. Theta accelerating on Sep 2 expiry. Locking in ~$1,360 loss rather than risk full position deterioration. Selling the spread for ~$1.40 credit (bid/ask: $716C at $2.71 bid, $720C at $1.30 ask, net ~$1.41 credit).

Attempting to close QQQ $716/$720C bull call spread via matching the original leg structure. Two failed intraday rally attempts (bounces to $715.84-$715.90 both rejected). QQQ now back at $714.09-$714.29, showing lower highs. Break-even at expiry requires QQQ at $717.76 — $3.50+ from current. Cutting loss of ~$1,360 to preserve capital.

QQQ is at $716.85 with a strong late-session bullish surge (up ~$2.50 from intraday lows). Buying the 717/720 bull call spread expiring Sep 1 to capture overnight continuation of this bullish momentum. QQQ needs to be at only $718.37 at tomorrow's close for full profitability — just a $1.52 move from current price. Using Sep 1 expiration specifically to avoid 0DTE time constraint (market closes in 6 min) while still capitalizing on the directional setup. Debit of $1.37, max loss $137/contract × 20 = $2,740 (2.8% of equity — well within limits). The consistent upward price action in the last 2 hours of August 31 is the directional signal.

QQQ has dropped ~$10 from $717 to $707 in a single session. The pre-market selloff was sharp but QQQ has been consolidating around $706.80-708 for the past hour since the open, suggesting exhaustion of selling momentum. This ATM bull call spread (buy $707C/sell $715C, Sep 3 expiry) profits on any recovery over the next 2 trading days. Break-even is ~$710.17 (only needs +$3 from current), max profit if QQQ reaches $715+. Net debit of ~$3.17 on an $8-wide spread. Risk is ~3.4% of equity — appropriate size. Bearish momentum appears to be stalling at current levels, and a relief rally on a -1.4% day is a historically plausible setup.

QQQ has bounced strongly from a $705.62 intraday low and is now at $708.91, clearly recovering. My existing 707/715 spread (8 contracts) is profitable (+$224 unrealized). Adding a complementary 709/716 bull call spread for Sep 3 expiry (5 contracts) increases my upside exposure to the continuing recovery. Buy QQQ709C (bid $3.65, ask $3.74, delta 0.496) and sell QQQ716C (bid $1.00, ask $1.07, delta 0.210). Net debit ~$2.74, spread width $7, break-even at $711.74. Total additional risk: $1,370 (~1.4% of equity). Combined risk from both spreads: ~$3,906 (~4.1% of equity). QQQ needs to reach $711.74+ to profit on this second spread — only $2.83 above current price. NVDA also rising ($218.50), confirming broad tech recovery. The intraday reversal is clean and momentum is sustained upward.

Closing the 707/715 Sep 3 call spread to lock in gains. The spread is essentially at max value ($4.80 vs theoretical max $4.83 at QQQ ≥$715). QQQ is at $712.22 — nearly at the short strike. With QQQ having just broken to new session highs, the spread has nearly fully realized its potential. Taking profit now captures ~$1,300 gain (41% of capital at risk) and eliminates the risk of a QQQ reversal eroding these gains. Selling the long 707C and buying back the short 715C at a net credit of ~$4.65.

Opening QQQ 712/720 Sep 3 call spread. QQQ at $711.48 with strong bullish momentum all afternoon — rallied from $705 lows to $712 highs on consistent buying. The 712/720 spread: buy 712C (~$3.43) sell 720C (~$0.74) for net debit ~$2.69-2.75. Break-even $714.69-$714.75, max gain $5.25-5.31 per contract. QQQ needs only ~$3 more rally to reach break-even with 2 full trading days remaining. This complements the existing 709/716 position by adding more upside exposure while keeping risk well within limits (~$2,750 total risk = 2.8% of equity). The prior 707/715 spread was closed at near-max gain, freeing capital for a fresh entry with a higher break-even that captures the next leg of a potential rally.

Closing the 712/720 Sep 3 call spread. QQQ has dropped ~$7.50 from our $711.50 entry to ~$704 pre-market. With expiry tomorrow (Sep 3), the 712C and 720C are deeply OTM and essentially worthless. Break-even would require QQQ to rally $10.75 in one day — essentially impossible. Closing to salvage any remaining value (estimated ~$0.30 net) and stop further theta decay. Selling the spread back: buy 720C (near zero) and sell 712C (small residual value ~$0.30). Net credit received will be small but better than letting both legs expire worthless and losing the full $2,750 premium paid.

Closing the 709/716 Sep 3 call spread. QQQ at ~$704, down ~$7.50 from entry area of $711.50. Break-even requires QQQ to rally to $712.64 by tomorrow's close — a $8.64 move in 1 day. Both legs deeply OTM. The 709C has small residual value (~$0.50-0.70 estimated) and 716C near zero (~$0.05-0.10). Closing to recover whatever residual value remains in the long 709C leg. Net credit expected ~$0.50-0.60 against original $2.64 cost. Taking the ~$2.10 loss per spread now rather than letting theta decay take it to zero by expiry tomorrow.

Opening NVDA Sep 4 217.5/225 call spread. NVDA showing strong relative strength: flat overnight (-$0.60) while QQQ dropped $7.50. Pre-market bars show tight range $216.54-$217.26, orderly and controlled. Yesterday's Sep 4 option chain shows very liquid strikes: 217.5C (26K vol), 220C (59K vol), 225C (43K vol). Net debit ~$2.46-2.80 (accounting for potential IV expansion). Break-even ~$220.26 — NVDA needs only $3.42 rally from pre-market $216.84 over 2 trading days. Width $7.50, max gain $4.70/contract, max risk $2.80/contract. 10 contracts = $2,800 total risk (2.9% of $94,960 equity). This is an attractive risk/reward with clear relative strength catalyst.

QQQ is in a clear pre-market downtrend, trading ~$704 — down ~$4 from yesterday's $707.85 close. A bear call spread (sell $710C/buy $715C) for Sep 11 expiry profits if QQQ stays below $710 through next Friday. With QQQ at $704, the short $710C leg is ~$6 OTM, giving reasonable probability of expiring worthless. Setting a conservative $1.50 net credit limit (~$150/contract, $350 max loss per contract on a $5-wide spread) so the order only fills if realistic market pricing at session open confirms the credit. 8 contracts × $350 max loss = $2,800 total risk = ~2.9% of equity. Action=open because this is a brand new position, not related to my existing QQQ Sep 3 spread which has separate pending close orders.

QQQ bear call spread for Sep 11 expiry. QQQ is at $706.71 at market open, with the $710 short strike $3.29 OTM. Pre-market showed a high of $708.25 before pulling back, suggesting $710 has real near-term resistance. With 9 days to expiry, theta will work in favor. Looking for at least $1.20 credit on the $5-wide spread. Max loss per contract = ($5.00 - $1.20) × 100 = $380. Action is 'open' as this is a new position — no Sep 11 spread currently held. Note: cannot verify exact Sep 11 ATM chain due to pagination limit cutting off at $683 strike, but extrapolating from Sep 3 pricing ($710C at $2.60-$2.70 with 1 day left), Sep 11 should have significantly more premium, making $1.20 credit realistic for this spread.

Closing the QQQ Sep 3 $712/$720 bull call spread before tomorrow's expiry. QQQ is at $707, with the $712 long call $5 OTM and only 1 day left — this spread is very unlikely to recover. Current mid value is ~$1.09 ($1.21 long - $0.12 short). Closing at -$1.05 credit (buying the $720C back at $0.12, selling the $712C at ~$1.17) recovers roughly $1,050 of the remaining value before the spread expires worthless. The action is 'close' — this reduces an existing losing long spread position. Max remaining loss per contract is $800 (original cost of $2.71 - current value ~$1.09 = $1.62 if we let expire, but selling now at $1.05 saves ~$1,050 total).

Closing QQQ Sep 3 $712/$720 bull call spread before tomorrow's expiration. QQQ at $706.20 is $5.80 below the $712 long strike — this spread expires worthless tomorrow. Current value is ~$0.78 (long at $0.85, short at $0.07). Closing now at -$0.75 credit recovers ~$750 before the entire position goes to zero at expiry. Previous close attempt was locked by a pending order; that order may have expired as a day order, so retrying now. This is a close action on an existing losing long spread.

Closing the NVDA Sep 4 $217.50/$225 bull call spread to lock in significant profit. NVDA has rallied from entry ~$218 to $221.50 today, making the $217.50C deeply ITM at $5.37 bid vs the $225C short now at $1.30. Net spread value is ~$4.07 vs entry cost of $2.79, yielding +$1,280 unrealized profit (+46%). Closing now at -$3.90 net credit (buying back the $225C at ~$1.31, selling the $217.50C at ~$5.21) locks in approximately $1,120-1,280 in profit. Risk of holding overnight into Friday expiry with NVDA needing $3.50 more to run to maximize at $225 outweighs the potential upside of an extra $200-400. This is action=close on the existing long bull call spread.

Closing the QQQ Sep 11 $710/$715 bear call spread (16 contracts) to limit losses. QQQ has bounced sharply from $705.30 to $708.11 in under 30 minutes, threatening the $710 short strike which is now only $1.89 away. The bear thesis is being challenged — QQQ showed strong buyers at the $705 level and is now recovering toward ATH. Entry credit was $2.14/contract ($3,424 total). Closing at $2.60 debit nets a ~$736 loss vs. max loss of $4,576 if QQQ breaks above $715. This is a defensive close to protect against a continuing rally. The NVDA spread was already closed for profit. This action=close on an existing short spread.

Opening NVDA Sep 11 $222.50/$230 bull call spread on strong intraday momentum. NVDA surged from $217.75 to $222+ on massive volume starting at 1:30 PM ET (1.76M shares in the first minute of the NYSE open, then 400-700K shares/min sustained for 35 minutes). Current price $221.92, holding gains firmly. This is the most active stock by trade count (434K trades today). Buying the $222.50C at ~$4.84, selling the $230C at ~$1.84 for $3.00 net debit. Spread is $7.50 wide. Max loss $300/contract = $3,000 total (3.1% of equity). Breakeven is $225.50, NVDA needs +1.6% from current levels over 9 days with strong bull momentum in play. The previous NVDA bull call spread (Sep 4 $217.50/$225) closed profitably with NVDA at $221-222, validating the bullish thesis. Sep 11 expiry gives 9 days for the move to play out.

Adding a second NVDA Sep 11 bull call spread at a higher strike level to capitalize on continued strong momentum. NVDA has surged from $217.75 to $224.10 today (+$6.35) on massive volume — #6 most active stock with 41M shares. The existing $222.50/$230 spread is now profitable (+$100) but I want to add incremental upside exposure via a higher-strike spread. Buying $225C (delta 0.486) at $4.00, selling $232.50C (delta 0.237) at $1.45 for net debit of $2.55. Breakeven is $227.55 (NVDA needs +$3.45 from current $224.10 level). Max loss $255/contract × 5 contracts = $1,275 (1.3% of equity). Combined NVDA exposure with existing spread: $4,275 max loss (4.5% of equity) — well within limits. Using small 5-contract size given NVDA has already moved significantly today, managing risk of chasing an extended name while still participating in the trend.

GOOGL showed a clear catalyst-driven spike at 10:12 AM ET from $337 to $339.56 on 339K shares (massive volume), then has been holding gains and trending higher in the ~$337-339 range. At $337.55, a $340/$350 BCS provides diversification away from NVDA concentration and gives 9 days for the catalyst momentum to push GOOGL above $340. GOOGL is #8 most active by trades (385K) indicating strong interest and liquidity. Net debit of $3.20 leaves 68% upside to max profit, and breakeven at $343.20 (+1.7% from current) is very achievable over 9 days. This diversifies the book with a non-semiconductor, non-NVDA tech name.

Closing today-expiring QQQ 712/720 call spread. QQQ is at ~$710, below the 712 long strike. The 712 calls still have $1.12 of value while the 720 short calls are nearly worthless at $0.03. Closing now captures ~$1,090 net remaining value rather than risking both legs expiring worthless if QQQ stays below 712 through close. This is a defensive close to salvage remaining value from a losing position.

META bull call spread 615/625 for 9/11 expiration. META is at ~$617.50, up strongly today with broad tech bullishness (NVDA, GOOGL, QQQ all up). Buying the 615C (delta 0.569, ATM) and selling the 625C (delta 0.451) for a net debit of ~$5.50. Breakeven at $620.50, with $10 spread width giving max gain of $4.50. The tight bid/ask spreads ($0.75 wide on the 615C, $0.70 wide on the 625C) confirm good liquidity. 8 days to expiry gives enough time for META to consolidate or continue higher. Max loss per contract $550, total risk 5 contracts = $2,750 (2.9% of equity). This diversifies beyond NVDA and GOOGL into another large-cap tech name showing bullish momentum.

Closing the META 615/625 bull call spread. META has been in a clear downtrend since peaking at $618.88 shortly after open, now at $611 and falling. The spread's long leg (615C) is now OTM with META at $611. Current spread value is approximately $3.75 (615C bid $10.75 minus 625C ask $7.62 = $3.13, or more conservatively $11.13 - $7.38 mid = $3.75). Entered at a net debit of $5.35; closing now for ~$3.75 limits the loss to ~$800 vs risking the full $2,675 max loss if META continues declining toward yesterday's close of $600. Closing to protect capital and avoid a larger loss as the intraday trend is clearly negative.

Closing the META 615/625 bull call spread. The previous close order at -$3.75 did not fill because the limit was too aggressive (market was offering ~$3.29-$3.49). META has been fading all day after a peak of $619 at the open, and is now consolidating around $612. The spread was entered at $5.35 debit and is now worth ~$3.49-3.95 in the market. Setting a limit of -$3.50 (net credit to us when closing) — this is at or slightly better than the current bid/ask crossover and should fill. Taking the loss now is better than holding through more potential downside. The remaining max loss on this position if held to expiry is ~$925 (already largely realized), vs. if META continues lower the remaining position value deteriorates further.

Opening a new NVDA 227.5/235 bull call spread for 5 contracts expiring 9/11. NVDA is at $226.69 and showing signs of stabilizing after a ~$2 intraday fade from $228+ highs. The 227.5C (delta 0.48) costs $3.74 ask; the 235C (bid $0.38) covers part of the cost. Net debit ~$3.36. NVDA needs only a $0.81 bounce to bring the long leg ATM. With 8 days to expiry and NVDA's strong underlying trend from $220 levels, this is a measured bullish play. The existing NVDA positions (222.5/230 and 225/232.5) are profitable; this adds incremental upside exposure at slightly higher strikes, positioned to benefit if NVDA resumes its upward trend toward $230+. Max loss $1,680 total (1.76% of equity), well within risk parameters.
